intro: A civil partner visa lets you join your civil partner in the UK if they are British, settled here, or have refugee or humanitarian protection. We prepare your civil partner visa application and check every document before it goes to the Home Office.

You both intend to live together permanently in the UK
You meet the financial requirement, through income, savings or a combination
You meet the English language requirement
You have suitable accommodation in the UK

sections.heading: Civil partner visa: who can apply?
sections.text:
The civil partner visa is part of the same family route as the spouse visa, and the requirements are the same. You can apply if you are in a civil partnership with a British citizen, an Irish citizen, someone settled in the UK, or someone with refugee or humanitarian protection.

Civil partnerships registered in the UK are recognised, and so are many relationships registered abroad that the UK treats as civil partnerships. Since December 2019, civil partnerships have also been open to opposite-sex couples in England and Wales, and the rest of the UK has since followed.

sections.heading: Is your overseas partnership recognised?
sections.text: If you registered your partnership outside the UK, it must be a relationship the UK recognises as a civil partnership or a marriage. Same-sex marriages are treated as marriages, so you would apply as a spouse instead. We check how your partnership is treated before you apply, so you use the right route.

sections.heading: Civil partner visa financial requirement in 2026
sections.text:
For most new applications, the UK partner must show a gross income of at least £29,000 a year. You can meet this through employment, self-employment, pensions, rental income or cash savings, and you can often combine them.

If you rely on savings alone, you need £88,500 for a first application. If your partner receives certain disability or carer's benefits, a different "adequate maintenance" test applies instead.

sections.heading: English, accommodation and evidence
sections.text:
You need English at A1 level for a first application, A2 when you extend, and B1 for settlement. You must also show suitable accommodation without public funds, and evidence that your relationship is genuine and continuing, such as photos together over time, messages, travel records and documents at a shared address.

If either of you was previously married or in a civil partnership, you need evidence it has legally ended, such as a divorce or dissolution order.

sections.heading: Planning to register your civil partnership in the UK?
sections.text: If you are not yet civil partners and want to register your partnership in the UK, you can apply for a proposed civil partner visa. It lasts 6 months, and you must register your partnership within that time. You then switch to a civil partner visa without leaving the UK. You can't work on a proposed civil partner visa.

sections.heading: From civil partner visa to settlement and citizenship
sections.text: A civil partner visa is granted for 2 years and 9 months from outside the UK, or 2 years and 6 months from inside. You then extend for a further 2 years and 6 months, and can usually apply for Indefinite Leave to Remain after 5 years. Once settled, you can apply for British citizenship after 3 years' residence, the same shorter route as for married couples.

faqs.q: Is a civil partner visa different from a spouse visa?
faqs.a: The requirements are the same, as both are part of the same family route. The main difference is the evidence: you provide your civil partnership certificate instead of a marriage certificate.

faqs.q: Can opposite-sex couples apply for a civil partner visa?
faqs.a: Yes. Civil partnerships have been open to opposite-sex couples in England and Wales since December 2019, and across the UK since then. The visa requirements are the same.

faqs.q: How long does a civil partner visa take?
faqs.a: Applications from outside the UK are usually decided within about 12 weeks, and from inside the UK within about 8 weeks. Priority services are available in some countries.

faqs.q: Can my civil partner work in the UK?
faqs.a: Yes. A civil partner visa lets your partner work and study in the UK. They can’t claim most public funds while on the visa.
